qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Installed base of ~23,000 locomotives provides captive aftermarket parts and services. However, returns on invested capital are structurally sub-hurdle (5-year median GAAP ROIC of 7.23%, with every year since the 2019 GE Transportation merger below 10%) due to $14B of merger goodwill/intangibles and immense countervailing buyer power from consolidated Class I freight railroads operating under Precision Scheduled Railroading.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 7.2% < 12%, REJECT). While Wabtec holds an entrenched North American locomotive installed base supporting recurring aftermarket service, its GAAP ROIC is structurally depressed (5-year median 7.23%, failing the 12% hurdle every year over the past 9 years). Concentrated Class I freight railroad buyers exert strong procurement leverage and maintain long asset lifecycles, constraining autonomous pricing power and returns on capital.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial track record reflects 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 7.23% (2021: 4.96%, 2022: 5.60%, 2023: 7.23%, 2024: 9.36%, 2025: 9.69%), failing the 12% hurdle. The 2019 GE Transportation acquisition brought $14.05B of goodwill and intangibles onto the balance sheet against $11.14B in equity. While FY2025 revenue grew to $11.17B and owner FCF reached $1.42B (conversion 1.35x), freight railroad customer concentration (Class I railroads generate the vast majority of freight sales, which are ~72% of total revenue) limits pricing power above inflation over the replacement cycle.
